claims.claim: Ordered-bipartition criterion: a bipartite n-vertex tree with classes A={x1,...,xa} and B={y1,...,yb} has a bipartition-separated graceful labeling if and only if the two classes can be ordered so that the endpoint-rank sums i+j over edges xiyj are pairwise distinct.
claims.evidence: Complement a separated labeling if necessary so A is the lower class. It then receives exactly 1,...,a; ordering A increasingly and B decreasingly gives |phi(x_i)-phi(y_j)|=n+1-(i+j). Conversely, orders with distinct sums yield the separated bijection phi(x_i)=i, phi(y_j)=n+1-j. The n−1 sums lie in the n−1-element set {2,...,n}, so they and the resulting differences are exactly the required sets.
claims.search_method: Direct bidirectional algebraic proof, including reversal of the low/high class by label complementation.
claims.witness: The mutually inverse construction is phi(x_i)=i and phi(y_j)=n+1-j, with edge difference n+1-i-j.

claims.claim: For every caterpillar, the bipartition orders described in the final writeup give endpoint-rank sums 2,3,...,n in succession.
claims.evidence: Writing ell_i=|L_i|, the t-th leaf edge at v_i has rank sum i+t+sum_{h<i}ell_h, one more than its position in the stated traversal. The following spine edge has sum i+1+sum_{h<=i}ell_h, again one more than its position. This covers both parities and empty leaf blocks, proving succession from 2 through n. The checker additionally confirmed the formula on every generated caterpillar through order 15.
claims.search_method: Symbolic rank calculation for arbitrary leaf-block sizes, supplemented by exact finite generation and validation.
claims.witness: For traversal position m, the construction gives endpoint-rank sum m+1; the n−1 positions therefore give 2,...,n.

claims.evidence: Claims 0 and 1 give a separated graceful labeling for every caterpillar with at least three vertices. K1 and K2 are immediate. The checker independently instantiated and validated the construction for every caterpillar through 15 vertices.
claims.search_method: Deduction from the verified ordered-bipartition criterion and general caterpillar rank formula, with exact finite validation.
claims.witness: Order the two classes as stated and assign ranks p in A label p and ranks q in B label n+1−q.

claims.claim: Extreme-vertex leaf-extension lemma: if a graceful n-vertex tree has a vertex v labeled 1, attaching any s≥0 new leaves at v preserves gracefulness.
claims.evidence: Keep the original labels and assign the new leaves n+1,...,n+s. Their incident differences from label 1 are n,...,n+s−1, disjoint from the original differences 1,...,n−1. All labels and all required differences occur exactly once; s=0 is included. The checker also tested extensions of every generated witness through order 15 for s=0,1,2,3.
claims.search_method: Direct exact formula for arbitrary s, supplemented by exact finite tests.
claims.witness: New leaf z_t receives phi(z_t)=n+t, producing difference n+t−1 for 1≤t≤s.

claims.claim: For every r≥0, the tree obtained from the once-subdivided K1,3 by adjoining r additional leaves to its center is a graceful non-caterpillar.
claims.evidence: The stated seven labels give differences 6,4,5,1,3,2. Center leaves labeled 8,...,7+r add exactly differences 7,...,6+r. Thus the 7+r labels and 6+r edge differences are complete and distinct for every r. The non-leaves c,u1,u2,u3 induce K1,3, so their induced subtree is not a path. Exact instances r=0,...,32 were also validated.
claims.search_method: Symbolic verification for arbitrary r, with exact integer instance checks.

claims.claim: The once-subdivided K1,3 has no bipartition-separated graceful labeling; hence not every tree admits the stronger alpha-type labeling used for caterpillars.
claims.evidence: After complementation, assume A={c,w1,w2,w3} is lower. If c has rank 1, 2, 3, or 4, its three sums are respectively {2,3,4}, {3,4,5}, {4,5,6}, or {5,6,7}. Requiring the missing extreme sums on leaf edges uniquely consumes rank pairs and leaves respectively 5 instead of 6, 5 instead of 6, 4 instead of 3, or minimum 4 instead of 3. Thus all four cases fail. Independently, the checker exhausted all 144 pairs of class orders and found zero with six distinct sums.
claims.search_method: Complete four-case rank proof and exhaustive permutation search over 4!·3! class orders.
claims.witness: For H with edges cu_i and u_iw_i (i=1,2,3), the exhaustive count of bipartition-separated rank orders is 0 of 144.

Sorted recursive child-code tuples are complete rooted-tree invariants by induction. Isomorphisms preserve the unique center or central edge, and the tagged center-rooted code therefore classifies unrooted trees exactly. Deduplication by that code leaves precisely one representative. claims.claim: For n≥2, in searching for a graceful labeling, it is complete to guess an edge, give its endpoints labels 0 and n−1 in one orientation, and search the remaining labels.
claims.evidence: A graceful n-vertex tree has n−1 distinct positive differences drawn from {1,...,n−1}, so difference n−1 must occur. Only labels 0 and n−1 realize it, hence they lie on an edge. Complementation l↦n−1−l reverses their orientation while preserving every difference, making one fixed orientation per guessed edge complete.
claims.search_method: Direct extremal-difference and complementation proof, implemented in the exhaustive checker.
claims.witness: Every validated n≥2 witness contained an edge whose label set was {0,n−1}.

claims.claim: The singleton tree K1 is graceful under its unique 0-based labeling, despite having no edge.
claims.evidence: The sole label 0 is a bijection onto {0}; the empty collection of edge differences is pairwise distinct. Shifting by one gives the target convention. The checker handles this case separately and validates it.
claims.search_method: Direct definition check and exact base-case execution.
claims.witness: V(K1)={v}, phi(v)=0, and the edge-difference multiset is empty.

claims.claim: The persisted backtracking and validation procedure is exact: every reported witness is graceful, and its pruning rules cannot remove a possible completion.
claims.evidence: Extreme-edge seeding is complete by claim 7. Assigned vertices remain connected, so a boundary vertex has exactly one assigned neighbor; all feasible unused labels for its single resolved edge are enumerated. A boundary with no feasible label cannot be completed. Likewise, every still-missing difference in any completion must be realizable on some unresolved edge using its fixed/free or free/free endpoint labels, so the second prune is necessary. At termination the validator separately requires labels {0,...,n−1} and differences {1,...,n−1}. The completed run exercised this procedure without any validation failure.
claims.search_method: Line-by-line logical audit of seeding, branching, both pruning conditions, and terminal validation, followed by exact execution.

claims.claim: Any counterexample to the graceful tree conjecture must have at least 16 vertices and contain a vertex adjacent to at least three non-leaf vertices.
claims.evidence: Claim 11 excludes orders at most 15, while claim 2 excludes caterpillars. For a tree of order at least three, its non-leaves induce a connected subtree because every internal vertex on a path between non-leaves has at least two neighbors. If every vertex had at most two non-leaf neighbors, that induced subtree would be a path, making the tree a caterpillar. The contrapositive gives the asserted branching vertex. The checker also verified this structural condition for every generated non-caterpillar.
claims.search_method: Logical combination of the finite certification and caterpillar theorem with a direct induced-subtree contrapositive; supplemented by exact finite checks.
claims.witness: Any remaining candidate must have n≥16 and its induced subtree on non-leaves must have maximum degree at least 3.

target_evidence: The exact target requires either a proof that every finite tree is graceful or an explicit finite nongraceful tree with a rigorous impossibility proof. The draft supplies neither: its seven-vertex example is explicitly graceful and only obstructs the stronger bipartition-separated labeling, while arbitrary non-caterpillars of order at least 16 remain untreated. Nevertheless, the caterpillar theorem, infinite graceful non-caterpillar family, alpha-labeling obstruction, exact certification through order 15, and resulting necessary structure for a counterexample are correct and material. Therefore the draft is VALID_PARTIAL_PROGRESS, not a full resolution. Its final writeup expressly states this limitation and claimed_resolution is PARTIAL, so that claimed resolution is ACCURATE.
